top_stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Scandal and Export Control Controversy
points: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder and only-ever CEO for 30-33 years, resigned effective immediately after reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman US intelligence allegedly identifies as a Chinese spy.
CFO Colette (also referred to as Nicole) Kress, who has a finance/MBA background rather than engineering, becomes interim CEO and will lead the company through next week's earnings report.
Nvidia's board stated it found 'no reason to believe that national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,' despite the espionage allegations.

Banned Nvidia chips (semiconductors restricted from export to China under US sanctions) were traced to a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, a Chinese entrepreneur; Singapore has charged a fifth person in a related export case.

Stock initially plunged as much as 14% before closing down 4.3%, as retail investors bought the dip in what one analyst called 'one of the more epic buy-the-news events in history'; shares are now down 25% over the past month.

At least six Wall Street analysts downgraded Nvidia, with Dan Ives cutting his price target from $300 to $225; however, Nvidia trades at just 11x forward 2027 earnings, cheaper than peers like Broadcom, TSMC, Alphabet, Microsoft, and AMD.

Lawmakers are demanding accountability, with Huang agreeing to testify before Congress under oath before Thanksgiving alongside Commerce Secretary Howard/Marco Lutnick regarding alleged illegal chip exports.
Silicon Valley is questioning whether Lutnick did enough to prevent advanced AI chips from reaching China, and the fallout could accelerate China's drive for semiconductor self-sufficiency.

unique_angles.point: Congressional demand for joint testimony from Lutnick and Huang signals lawmakers view this as a high-level governance failure requiring accountability from both private sector and government officials.

Nvidia exhibited extreme key-person risk with 60 employees reporting directly to Huang and no succession plan in place; prediction markets give Ian Buck, VP of hyperscale and high-performance computing, a 40% chance of becoming permanent CEO, while Trump suggested Tim Cook as an alternative.

Washington lawmakers are preparing to add the AI Overwatch Act, Chip Security Act, and MATCH Act to this year's defense bill ahead of Trump's planned meeting with Xi Jinping; Chinese AI firms are accelerating purchases of Nvidia chip capacity overseas before potential new export restrictions.

If Nvidia survives this crisis without Huang, the episode could strengthen the broader AI trade narrative by proving it doesn't depend on one visionary founder, drawing a direct parallel to Apple's successful transition from Steve Jobs to Tim Cook.
The smuggled chips were linked to Megaspeed International Pte., and Huang reportedly appeared visibly dejected in his final hours before ouster, a scene described as stunning Silicon Valley.

top_stories.title: Microsoft's Multi-Day Global Outage
points: Microsoft's outage affecting Outlook (email), Teams (collaboration/chat tool), and Copilot AI has persisted into a second day, far longer than most previous glitches which rarely exceed a few hours.
The outage has disrupted trading desks, forcing traders onto phones and alternative communication channels, and has paralyzed government offices and businesses worldwide.
Service restoration timelines remain uncertain, with productivity losses accumulating across organizations dependent on Microsoft's cloud and collaboration tools.

items.title: SpaceX Attempts Historic Full Rocket Reusability
points: SpaceX will attempt tonight (5:45-7:00 PM ET) to recover an entire Starship rocket for the first time, capturing the first stage (booster) minutes after liftoff and the second stage on Saturday—a feat never before accomplished.

Previous reusable rocket efforts recovered only first-stage boosters; second stages were left unrecovered because adding heat shields, landing legs, and grid fins would consume too much payload capacity relative to the booster's cost.
Starship's large size and cargo capacity make full reusability economically viable, potentially enabling it to eventually replace Falcon rockets for commercial and government missions.
Full reusability would support Elon Musk's long-term vision of lunar landings, point-to-point Earth transport, and Mars colonization by significantly reducing launch costs.

items.title: Anthropic IPO 6x Oversubscribed
points: Anthropic's IPO (initial public offering, when a private company first sells shares to the public) received 6x oversubscription, meaning demand was six times the available share supply.
The IPO is set to debut next week, adding another major AI company to public markets amid investor enthusiasm for generative AI despite valuation concerns.

Although China tightened chemical regulations, large-scale shipments of fentanyl precursors and new synthetic opioids continue.

headlines: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after revelations of affairs including one with alleged Chinese spy; CFO Nicole Kress becomes interim CEO and will lead the company through earnings next week.
Nvidia stock fell 4.3% after initially dropping 14%, recovering as retail investors bought the dip in what one analyst called "one of the more epic buy-the-news events in history."

Wall Street cut price targets with Dan Ives lowering his from $300 to $225, valuing Huang's leadership at a 25% premium; analyst notes suggest Kress's business knowledge makes her a steady pair of hands.

If Nvidia successfully navigates this crisis, the AI trade could emerge stronger by proving it doesn't depend on a single visionary founder, similar to how Apple thrived after Steve Jobs under Tim Cook.

sections.title: The Nvidia Leadership Crisis: What Happened and Market Impact
points: Jensen Huang, CEO for 33 years, resigned after reports surfaced of multiple affairs including one with a woman US intelligence identifies as a Chinese spy, plus affairs with two Nvidia employees.
Nvidia exhibited extreme key-person risk: 60 employees reported directly to Huang with no succession plan and few public-facing managers ready to step into the top role.
Stock fell from initial 14% loss to 4.3% decline as retail investors aggressively bought the dip; Nvidia is now back to summer 2025 price levels, down 25% over the past month.
Prediction markets give Ian Buck, VP of hyperscale and high-performance computing, a 40% chance of becoming permanent CEO; President Trump suggested Tim Cook as an alternative.

sections.title: The Hidden Upside: Why Nvidia Could Emerge Stronger
points: If Nvidia survives this test without Huang, investors and analysts will evaluate the company on fundamentals and arguments alone, removing the 'rose-colored glasses' effect that visionary founders often create.

The parallel to Apple is instructive: after Steve Jobs' departure, Apple lost direction but eventually recovered and thrived under Tim Cook, proving the company and its business model were more durable than any single leader.
Huang's departure eliminates the cult of personality from the AI trade narrative, which could make the entire sector appear more rock-solid and less dependent on one individual's charisma or vision.
Successful transition would demonstrate the AI trade wasn't a one-man show propped up by Huang, potentially validating long-term secular growth assumptions investors are betting on.

sections.title: Congressional and Geopolitical Fallout
points: Huang agreed to testify before Congress under oath before Thanksgiving; the House Foreign Affairs chair is investigating the espionage allegations.
Democrats demanded Nvidia preserve all records, signaling the China scandal is just beginning despite Huang's departure and will shape Washington's approach to chip export controls.

The affair has shifted chip export policy from a wonky technocratic issue to the centerpiece of an alleged espionage scandal, with unclear implications given Nvidia's business interests align with China's import demand.
